resume: Findings in `unverified` with `refutersDispatched` above `refutersInconclusive` lost a refuter to a crash — a pair whose every vote died was re-dispatched once in-run and died again — and no refuter that ran decided them. Defer them as crashed — reported, not acted on: omp's eval has no cached-replay mechanism, so a fresh review re-dispatches every agent() live rather than only the crashed legs, and the in-run retry was this review's one re-dispatch. Re-run nothing for them.
testEnvironment:
Test environment: the snapshot is a git repository whose single commit holds
the reviewed tree — its tree hash was compared against the commit under review
when the snapshot was cut. A suite run here collects and runs what a checkout at
that commit does, so a failing or skipped test is a fact about the tree, not
about this copy of it. Its history is that one synthetic commit: 'git log',
'git diff' and every ancestry question answer about the snapshot and never about
the PR.
The Recipe's Test entrypoint and Check step do not run these merge-gating CI steps, and nothing in this review ran them: Verify branch is rebased on base (needs pull-request context and full git history, not the worktree); Validate renovate.json (fetches renovate from the npm registry via npx on every run); smoke-omp (needs bun and a globally installed pinned omp binary); install-and-smoke (needs bun and a globally installed pinned omp binary).

survived.claim: The PR makes resolveBot read top-level `cfg.digest` and `cfg.pinDigest` (via emittableTypes), but botShapeProblem still shape-checks only `[...Object.keys(SEGMENT_OF), "rollback"]`. A non-object top-level `"digest"` or `"pinDigest"` override therefore crashes every test with a raw TypeError instead of producing the problem naming renovate.json, which is the contract the shape guard exists to keep.
survived.evidence: In the copy: `node -e '…c.digest="x"…' && node --test tests/renovate-release-contract.test.mjs` gave `ℹ fail 12` and `TypeError [Error]: Cannot use 'in' operator to search for 'labels' in x` ×9. Control with `c.minor="x"` gave `ℹ fail 12` with `renovate.json: top-level \`minor\` override must be an object, got "x"`. renovate.json was restored with git checkout and `git status --porcelain -uall` was empty.
survived.suggested_fix: In botShapeProblem, iterate `[...Object.keys(SEGMENT_OF), ...DIGEST_TYPES, "rollback"]` (or emittableTypes' full vocabulary) so every type resolveBot reads as `cfg[type]` is shape-checked.

unverified.claim: The pin contract reads only `*.yml` (`.filter((name) => name.endsWith(".yml"))`). A `.github/workflows/*.yaml` workflow with unpinned tag refs, which GitHub Actions runs and Renovate's github-actions manager also covers, passes the suite green. The custom regex manager's managerFilePatterns has the same `.yml`-only scope.
unverified.evidence: In the copy: writing `.github/workflows/extra.yaml` containing `- uses: actions/checkout@v5` and `- uses: owner/unpinned@main`, then `node --test tests/workflow-action-pins.test.mjs`, gave `ℹ pass 7 ℹ fail 0`. The same content as `extra.yml` gave `ℹ fail 2` with `.github/workflows/extra.yml: \`uses: actions/checkout@v5\` is not pinned to a 40-hex commit SHA (ref \`v5\`)`. A JS probe of managerFilePatterns gives `.github/workflows/x.yaml false`. No `.yaml` workflow exists today, and the ticket words the rule over `*.yml`.
unverified.suggested_fix: Filter with `/\.ya?ml$/` in the test (and optionally in managerFilePatterns), or add an assertion that no `.yaml` workflow exists, so the scope cannot be bypassed silently.
